samples.question: The picture shows a board of 6 by 6 square cells drawn in grey. Five of the cells hold a coloured pad: one red, one blue, one purple, one teal and one yellow, each colour used once. A black triangle stands in another cell: that is the robot, and the robot stands in the cell whose square contains the triangle. The robot faces the way its apex, the sharp corner opposite its flat back edge, points; that facing is whichever of up, right, down or left the apex points closest to, where up means towards the top edge of the board, down towards the bottom edge, left towards the left edge and right towards the right edge. Below the board is a row of cream cards, carried out one at a time in order from left to right, as the grey arrow beneath the row shows. A card carrying a grey arrow and some black dots is a drive card: the robot moves straight ahead, in the direction it is facing at that moment, one cell for each black dot on that card, and its facing does not change. A card carrying a green bent arrow turns the robot a quarter turn to its own left, and a card carrying an orange bent arrow turns it a quarter turn to its own right; a turn card never moves the robot. The turns are made from the robot's point of view, so a turn card changes the direction every later drive card sends it: after a green card a robot that faced up faces left, and after an orange card a robot that faced up faces right. The grey arrow on a drive card points up on the card only to mark it as a drive card; it does not say which way the robot moves. No card ever takes the robot off the board, pads do not block or divert it, and it may pass over pads on the way. The robot is drawn only once, in its starting cell and starting facing: no later position or facing of the robot is drawn anywhere. After every card has been carried out, the robot stands on one of the five coloured pads. After every card has been carried out in order, which coloured pad is the robot standing on? Answer with one word: red, blue, purple, teal or yellow.
